comment: The machine v0.1 conformance floor. Accepts carry structural expectations (identity, counts, service start order, granted capability set, and where it matters the folded rationale); rejects carry the fragment the refusal must contain, so a runtime refusing for the wrong reason fails (exemplar gap G8, applied from birth). Three of the accepts are the three profiles a machine can declare: a hosted box, an edge sensor, a touch phone. v0.1 widened 2026-09-12 (OS-4) with the BOARD clause: A9, R33, R34, R35 are the board's own; A1 and A2 carry the defaulted and the declared board. Widened again 2026-09-12 (the NETWORK kind): A10, A11, R36-R40; A2 is the box file with its NETWORK; every accept's counts carry networks. Widened again 2026-09-12 (SLOTS, A/B): A12, R41, R42. Widened again 2026-09-12 (READY, a daemon's own signal): A13, R43, R44, R45. Widened again 2026-09-12 (USER, a declared identity): A14, R46-R50; every accept's counts carry users. Widened again 2026-09-12 (the edge boards): A3 becomes machines/cold_room_sensor.machine verbatim with BOARD pico2; A15, R51, R52; R35 now refuses a hosted board on an edge machine by profile. Widened again 2026-10-04 (FORWARD, the way between networks): A27-A29, R95-R103; a machine says it forwards, never assumes it, one network (and a loopback is not one) has nothing to forward between, a machine that forwards cannot say there is no way off a link it joins, and one machine answers for a domain once. Widened again 2026-10-05 (STATE, a world's own directory): A30-A35, R104-R138; a world that runs as an identity owns the directories it names and nothing else of the machine's, only an identity can own one, only where the machine can hand one over (under /run, or inside an ext4 or tmpfs mount the world keeps and that is not read-only, with every mount above it kept too), no two worlds own overlapping directories, a world's signal sits directly in its own directory and never in a neighbour's, the floor's own key and record are in no directory a world owns, and the paths the court compares are plain names of bounded length, so that no spelling reaches one file by two names. Two rules about mounts came with it, because a directory's holder is the innermost mount only if the outer one is declared first and no two share a mount point.

accepts.name: the minimal machine: one MACHINE declaration, defaults stated
accepts.source:
DEFINE MACHINE hello AS (
  PROFILE hosted,
  ARCH x86_64,
  KERNEL linux
) RATIONALE "The smallest declarable machine"

accepts.name: the hosted box: the counter machine of a restaurant, whole -- machines/makeen_box.machine verbatim
accepts.source:
-- makeen_box.machine -- the box behind the counter: server, network and
-- bridge in one. The hosted profile's reference machine (fixture A2 is
-- this file, verbatim) and, since OS-4, the board's truth: a Raspberry
-- Pi 4 Model B, the SD card's second partition as /data, the console on
-- the header pins, the network declared and brought up by PID 1 before
-- any world speaks, and two boot slots: an update is tried once under
-- the watchdog and committed only when every world is SERVING -- and
-- still serving a window later -- and the box recognises its own boot. RestoLean's Makeen thread named the box;
-- this declares it.

DEFINE MACHINE makeen_box AS (
  PROFILE hosted,
  ARCH aarch64,
  KERNEL linux,
  LIBC musl,
  BOARD rpi4,
  CONSOLE "/dev/ttyS1",
  SLOTS "/dev/mmcblk0p1",
  IDENTITY "/data/device.key",
  JOURNAL "/data/boot.journal"
) RATIONALE "One box, no shell, no package manager: the declared machine is the system; two slots, so an update is a trial before it is a commitment"

DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "The box is the restaurant's network"

DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "Orders and stock live on the box"

DEFINE CAPABILITY gpio AS (
  GRANT no
) RATIONALE "No pins on the counter box; sensors are edge machines"

DEFINE MOUNT data AS (
  AT "/data",
  FS ext4,
  DEVICE "/dev/mmcblk0p2",
  OPTIONS [rw, noatime]
) RATIONALE "The persistent partition: the SD card's second partition"

DEFINE NETWORK lan AS (
  INTERFACE "eth0",
  ADDRESS "192.168.10.1/24"
) RATIONALE "The box is the network's address; the phones find it here. No gateway: the box is the gateway"

DEFINE SERVICE kds AS (
  RUN ["/stzr", "/app/kds.luau"],
  RESTART always,
  READY "/run/kds.ready",
  HEALTH 5,
  NEEDS [network, filesystem]
) RATIONALE "The kitchen display world: a daemon that serves the kitchen and says so by creating its READY path; PID 1 keeps it alive for the life of the box"

DEFINE SERVICE poste AS (
  RUN ["/stzr", "/app/poste.luau"],
  RESTART always,
  READY "/run/poste.ready",
  HEALTH 5,
  AFTER [kds],
  NEEDS [network, filesystem]
) RATIONALE "The counter world: a daemon too, and it starts only once the kitchen display has SIGNALLED it is serving -- not merely started"

accepts.name: the edge sensor: no kernel, no libc, pins and a flash log -- machines/cold_room_sensor.machine verbatim
accepts.source:
-- cold_room_sensor.machine -- the edge profile's reference machine, and
-- fixture A3 verbatim: the HACCP probe of RestoLean's cold room, the
-- sensor the Makeen box listens to. It is declared here and PROJECTED
-- onto MicroRing's substrate (`harb project`), never imaged and never
-- booted here: `harb init` refuses the edge profile by name and says
-- whose it is. MicroRing owns the firmware, the tiers and the loop.

DEFINE MACHINE cold_room_sensor AS (
  PROFILE edge,
  ARCH thumbv8m,
  KERNEL none,
  BOARD pico2
) RATIONALE "A thermistor, a log, a radio: the binary is the device"

DEFINE CAPABILITY gpio AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "The probe and the LED are pins"

DEFINE CAPABILITY clock AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "Readings are timestamped"

DEFINE PIN led AS (
  GPIO 25,
  MODE out
) RATIONALE "Heartbeat: the board's own LED, so a cold room says it is alive"

DEFINE PIN probe AS (
  GPIO 4,
  MODE in
) RATIONALE "The thermistor"

DEFINE MOUNT log AS (
  AT "/log",
  FS littlefs,
  DEVICE "flash0"
) RATIONALE "Power-loss safe, wear-levelled: a reading survives the power going out"

DEFINE SERVICE sense AS (
  RUN ["sense"],
  RESTART always,
  NEEDS [gpio, clock]
) RATIONALE "Read, log, sleep -- the behaviour itself is the Device language's, projected as a named seam"

accepts.name: AFTER orders the services; declaration order breaks ties
accepts.source:

DEFINE SERVICE c AS (RUN ["c"], AFTER [a, b]) RATIONALE "third"
DEFINE SERVICE b AS (RUN ["b"], AFTER [a]) RATIONALE "second"
DEFINE SERVICE a AS (RUN ["a"]) RATIONALE "first"

accepts.name: comments anywhere, trailing commas everywhere, an empty list
accepts.source:

DEFINE MACHINE m AS ( -- after a paren
  PROFILE hosted, -- after a clause
  ARCH x86_64,
  KERNEL linux,
) RATIONALE "commas"
DEFINE CAPABILITY clock AS (GRANT yes,) RATIONALE "tick"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (
  RUN ["s", "--flag",],
  AFTER [],
  NEEDS [clock,],
) RATIONALE "lists"
-- a comment at the end, no newline

accepts.source:

) RATIONALE "It says when it is serving, not the kernel"

  RESTART never,

) RATIONALE "Starts on the signal, not on the spawn"

accepts.name: a declared identity, and a service that runs as it

DEFINE USER kds AS (
  UID 1000,
  GID 1000
) RATIONALE "The kitchen display world owns nothing of the machine"
DEFINE USER poste AS (
  UID 1001
) RATIONALE "The counter world; its gid follows its uid unless declared"

  RUN ["/display"],
  USER kds,
  NEEDS [process]
) RATIONALE "Runs as the identity, not as the machine"

  PROFILE hosted,

accepts.name: the box is the network's server of names: a declared peer has an address and a name that keeps it

accepts.name: each world keeps the storage it was given and not the rest
accepts.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY process AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS tmpfs, OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT logs AS (AT "/var/log", FS tmpfs, OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE ledger AS (
  RUN ["/w"],
  RESTART never,
  NEEDS [process, filesystem],
  SEES [data]
) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE printer AS (
  RUN ["/w"],
  RESTART never,
  AFTER [ledger],
  NEEDS [process, filesystem],
  SEES [logs]
) RATIONALE "x"

  CONSOLE "/dev/ttyS0"
) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: is not a console of BOARD qemu_virt

rejects.name: the kernel's name for a port is not its device: CONSOLE names the device PID 1 speaks on
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (
  PROFILE hosted,
  ARCH x86_64,
  KERNEL linux,
  CONSOLE "ttyS0"
) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: is not a console of BOARD qemu_pc

rejects.name: forwarding between networks is a hosted machine's declaration: an edge machine is the way between nothing
rejects.source: DEFINE MACHINE s AS (PROFILE edge, ARCH thumbv7em, KERNEL none, FORWARD yes) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: FORWARD is a hosted machine's declaration

rejects.name: a machine that is not the way between networks declares nothing, never `FORWARD no`
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, FORWARD no) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK front AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.20.1/24") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK core AS (INTERFACE "eth1", ADDRESS "10.20.0.1/24") RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: FORWARD takes a word, not a string
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, FORWARD "yes") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK front AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.20.1/24") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK core AS (INTERFACE "eth1", ADDRESS "10.20.0.1/24") RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: one network has nothing to forward between
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, FORWARD yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK front AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.20.1/24") RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: and it declares 1: a machine with fewer than two networks has nothing to forward between

rejects.name: no network at all has nothing to forward between either
rejects.source: DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, FORWARD yes) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: and it declares 0: a machine with fewer than two networks has nothing to forward between

rejects.name: a loopback is a network a machine declares and not a way to anywhere: one wire and a loopback is one link
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, FORWARD yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK loopback AS (INTERFACE "lo", ADDRESS "127.0.0.1/8") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK front AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.20.1/24") RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: and it declares 1: a machine with fewer than two networks has nothing to forward between (a loopback is not a way to anywhere)

rejects.name: a machine that forwards is a way off every link it joins, so it cannot say EGRESS none for one of them
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux, FORWARD yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK front AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.20.1/24") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK core AS (INTERFACE "eth1", ADDRESS "10.20.0.1/24", EGRESS none) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: a machine that forwards is a way off every link it joins

rejects.name: a ROUTE belongs to a fleet file: which links are joined is a fact about a set, and no machine can say it
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE ROUTE r AS (BETWEEN [front, core], THROUGH gw) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: ROUTE belongs to a fleet file, not a machine file

rejects.name: two networks of one machine answering to the same domain: a name on one link would be a name on both
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE gw AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK front AS (INTERFACE "eth0", ADDRESS "192.168.20.1/24", DOMAIN "cloud") RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE NETWORK core AS (INTERFACE "eth1", ADDRESS "10.20.0.1/24", DOMAIN "cloud") RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: core serves cloud, which front already serves

rejects.name: a directory is owned by an identity: a world with no USER is the machine itself, and a place made for it is made for nobody
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, STATE ["/run/s"]) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: an empty STATE says nothing: a world that keeps nothing of its own declares none
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE []) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: an empty STATE is not a declaration

rejects.name: STATE takes paths in strings, not words
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE [data]) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: STATE takes a list of paths in strings

rejects.name: a relative path is a place nobody can name
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE ["run/s"]) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: STATE is an absolute path of plain names

rejects.name: a path that climbs is a path to somewhere else: .. is refused wherever it stands
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE ["/run/../etc/s"]) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: STATE is an absolute path of plain names

rejects.name: a trailing slash names the same directory twice over
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE ["/run/s/"]) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: STATE is an absolute path of plain names

rejects.name: an empty name between slashes is not a name
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE ["/run//s"]) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: STATE is an absolute path of plain names

rejects.name: the image's own directories are the machine's: a world owns a place under /run or on a mount it keeps, nowhere else
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE ["/etc/s"]) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: is in no place a world may own

rejects.name: /run is the machine's scratch directory, and a world owns a directory INSIDE it, never it
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE ["/run"]) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: the root of a MOUNT is the machine's too: a world that owned it would own every other world's place on it
rejects.source:

DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS ext4, DEVICE "/dev/vda", OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, NEEDS [filesystem], USER srv, STATE ["/data"]) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a world that did not declare the filesystem has none of the machine's storage in its tree, so it cannot own a place there
rejects.source:

DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS ext4, DEVICE "/dev/vda", OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, USER srv, STATE ["/data/s"]) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a world that narrows its sight cannot own a place on the mount it narrowed away
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS ext4, DEVICE "/dev/vda", OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"

DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: nothing can be made on a mount that is read-only
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (GRANT yes) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS ext4, DEVICE "/dev/vda", OPTIONS [ro]) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, NEEDS [filesystem], USER srv, STATE ["/data/s"]) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: a filesystem that keeps no owners cannot hand a directory to an identity

DEFINE MOUNT card AS (AT "/card", FS vfat, DEVICE "/dev/mmcblk0p1", OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"

DEFINE MOUNT data AS (AT "/data", FS ext4, DEVICE "/dev/vda", OPTIONS [rw]) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: two worlds cannot own the same directory
rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER oth AS (UID 2001) RATIONALE "x"

DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"

DEFINE USER oth AS (UID 2001) RATIONALE "x"

DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"

DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, READY "/run/s.ready", USER srv) RATIONALE "x"

rejects.name: and a signal that is the directory itself would be true before the world had done anything

DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, READY "/run/s", USER srv, STATE ["/run/s"]) RATIONALE "x"
rejects.refusal: which is not directly in a directory it owns

rejects.source:
DEFINE MACHINE m AS (PROFILE hosted, ARCH x86_64, KERNEL linux) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE USER srv AS (UID 2000) RATIONALE "x"
DEFINE SERVICE s AS (RUN ["/s"], RESTART always, READY "/run/s/ready", USER srv, STATE ["/run/s"]) RATIONALE "x"
